Evidence must be OBSERVED against https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp and recorded in a ticket comment naming the tool called, the arguments, and the actual response.
findings.detail: The ticket's Phase 2 comment explicitly states 'AC17 LIVE VALIDATION — NOT MET. Pending deployment.' and records only the BEFORE evidence (the unfixed error response). No subsequent comment in the ticket snapshot records the AFTER evidence — a successful call to the deployed endpoint post-redeployment naming the tool, arguments, and actual response. The description checkbox text contains an inline attestation ('bridge_status returned a structured verdict (verdict=FOREIGN, record_oid present) with NO .env-id ... No such file or directory error'), but this lacks the required specifics: no timestamp of when the call was made post-deployment, no explicit confirmation that the container had redeployed with the fix. The ticket's own comments — the authoritative record — show only the before-state, and the Phase 2 comment explicitly marks this as not met.
findings.remediation: After the fix is deployed and the container restarts, call bridge_status through https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp and record a ticket comment naming: (1) the tool called (bridge_status), (2) the arguments ({}), (3) the actual response showing a structured verdict with no .env-id ENOENT error, and (4) the timestamp of the call. This comment constitutes the required AC17 evidence.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
